'''Peter Philip Edwards''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 1949, Liverpool) is a British Emeritus Professor of [[Inorganic Chemistry]] and former Head of Inorganic Chemistry at the [[University of Oxford]] and a Fellow of [[St Catherine's College, Oxford]].<ref name='WhosWho'>{{cite web|url = http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U14715|title = EDWARDS, Prof. Peter Philip | accessdate = 2012-07-31|date = 2012|work = Who's Who 2012 online edition|publisher = A & C Black}}</ref> Edwards is the recipient of the [[Corday-Morgan Medal]] (1985),<ref name='RSC CM'>{{cite web | url = http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/CordayMorganPrizes/PreviousWinners.asp | title = Corday-Morgan Medal and Prize Winners | accessdate = 2014-04-15}}</ref> the Tilden Lectureship (1993–94)<ref name='RSC Tild'>{{cite web | url = http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/TildenPrizes/PreviousWinners.asp | title = Tilden Lectureships Winners|accessdate = 2014-04-15}}</ref> and Liversidge Award (1999)<ref name='RSC Liv'>{{cite web | url = http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/LiversidgeAward/PreviousWinners.asp|title = Liversidge Award Winners|accessdate = 2014-04-15}}</ref> of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]. He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1996 and was awarded the 2003 [[Hughes Medal]] of the Royal Society <ref name='Hughes Medal'>{{cite web | url = https://royalsociety.org/awards/hughes-medal/ |title = Hughes Medal Winners|accessdate = 2014-04-16}}</ref> "for his distinguished work as a solid state chemist. He has made seminal contributions to fields including superconductivity and the behaviour of metal nanoparticles, and has greatly advanced our understanding of the phenomenology of the metal-insulator transition". In 2009 Edwards was elected to the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]],<ref name='List of Members'>{{cite web | url = http://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/1368/ | title = List of Members: Prof. Dr. Peter P. Edwards | accessdate = 2014-04-15}}</ref>  and he was elected Einstein Professor for 2011 by the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://english.cas.cn/IC/AF/200909/t20090917_38980.shtml | title = Einstein Professorship Program | accessdate = 2014-04-14 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131011113704/http://english.cas.cn/IC/AF/200909/t20090917_38980.shtml | archive-date = 2013-10-11 | url-status = dead }}</ref> In 2012 he was awarded the [[Bakerian Lecture]] by the Royal Society "in recognition of decisive contributions to the physics, chemistry and materials science of condensed matter, including work on the metal-insulator transition".<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.ox.ac.uk/media/news_stories/2011/110719.html | title = Royal Society award winners | accessdate = 2014-04-15 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140517123809/http://www.ox.ac.uk/media/news_stories/2011/110719.html | archive-date = 2014-05-17 | url-status = dead }}</ref> In the spring of 2012 he was elected International Member of the [[American Philosophical Society]];<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Edwards;smode=advanced;f1-subdiv=102.%20Chemistry%20and%20Chemical%20Biochemistry | title = American Philosophical Society Member History: Professor Peter P. Edwards | accessdate = 2014-04-16}}</ref> one of only four people from the UK in that year to be awarded this honour across all subjects and disciplines. Later in 2012 he was awarded the [[Worshipful Company of Armourers and Brasiers]] Materials Science Venture Prize for his work on new, low-cost, high-performance conducting oxide coatings for solar cells and optoelectronic materials.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.armourershall.co.uk/venture-prize-winners/ | title = Materials Science Venture Prize Winners | accessdate = 2014-04-14 | archive-date = 25 May 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170525214016/http://www.armourershall.co.uk/venture-prize-winners/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> In the Autumn of 2013 he was elected Member of [[Academia Europaea]],<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Edwards_Peter_Philip | title = Academia Europaea Members | accessdate = 2014-04-14}}</ref> and he was elected as a Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2014.<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web |url=https://www.amacad.org/multimedia/pdfs/classlist2014.pdf |title=Newly Elected Members |publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] |date=April 2014 |accessdate=2014-05-16 }}</ref><ref name="OxMailAAAS">{{cite news |title=Honour for academics |work=[[Oxford Mail]] |date=2014-05-29 |page=17 }}</ref>

Together with Tiancun Xiao and John Thomas and their teams Edwards demonstrated in 2020 a new method using microwaves to initiate the catalytic decomposition of [[plastic waste]] to generate hydrogen and multiwalled carbon nanotubes.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lopez |first1=Gartzen |last2=Santamaria |first2=Laura |title=Microwaving plastic into hydrogen and carbons |journal=Nature Catalysis |date=2020 |volume=3 |issue=11 |pages=861–862 |doi=10.1038/s41929-020-00538-1|s2cid=226308787 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Whipple |first1=Tom |title=Microwaves could turn plastic waste into hydrogen fuel |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/environment/article/microwaves-could-turn-plastic-waste-into-hydrogen-fuel-bdq76xhjd |access-date=5 September 2022 |work=[[The Times]] |date=17 October 2020}}</ref> This approach was subsequently developed by the [[University spin-off|spin-out company]] Oxford Sustainable Fuels.<ref>{{cite news |title=Oxford Sustainable Fuels to tackle plastic crisis by recycling waste into fuels |url=https://www.energymanagermagazine.co.uk/oxford-sustainable-fuels-to-tackle-plastic-crisis-by-recycling-waste-into-fuels/ |access-date=5 September 2022 |work=Energy Manager Magazine}}</ref> {{As of|2022}} Edwards was working with CarbonMeta Technologies to commercialise the approach.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kelly |first1=Amelia |title=Oxford trial turns plastic waste to hydrogen fuel |url=https://resource.co/article/oxford-trial-turns-plastic-waste-hydrogen-fuel |access-date=5 September 2022 |work=Resource Magazine |date=4 July 2022}}</ref> He is a founder of and scientific consultant for OXCCU.<ref>{{cite web |title=Our Leadership Team |url=https://www.oxccu.com/about |publisher=OXCCU |access-date=11 May 2026}}</ref>
